findings.title: Pagination creates an extra empty page for exact page-size totals
findings.body: `totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which is one too high whenever the member count is an exact multiple of the page size. For example, a group with 50 members and a limit of 50 is displayed as having two pages; clicking next requests offset 50 and renders an empty member list. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (while retaining the zero-member special case) so the navigation and `showingLast` state match the available results.

findings.title: Public member-list pagination accepts an unbounded client-controlled limit
findings.body: The `members` endpoint applies `params[:limit].to_i` directly to the relation and serializes every selected user. Any user allowed to see a group (including an anonymous user for visible groups) can request an arbitrarily large limit and force loading and serializing the entire membership in one response. Clamp the limit to a reasonable maximum and normalize invalid/non-positive values; this also avoids malformed values causing database offset/limit errors.

findings.title: Out-of-order member requests can replace the currently selected page
findings.body: Each `findMembers` completion unconditionally writes `offset`, `members`, and pagination metadata to the shared group model. If a user clicks next and then previous before the first request finishes, the previous-page request can complete first and the stale next-page response can complete afterward, leaving the UI on the wrong page while the model offset no longer reflects the user's latest action. Cancel superseded requests or associate a request/version token with each load and ignore stale responses.
